why_ai: Network-effect platforms persist, but their engineering and enforcement work is already run by models.
why_clarity: Billions of near-identical decisions, but viewer value and enforcement correctness go unvalidated.
why_digital: Uploads, recommendation, delivery and advertising are entirely online.

why_ai: Income-changing reversals need accountable human review, though triage and reviewer support automate.
why_clarity: Appeals arrive at huge volume, but whether a reversal was right is rarely checked.
why_digital: Appeal cases reviewed in platform tooling against digital content.

why_ai: Fair use and adversarial broad claiming need legal judgment, but matching and scoring are automated.
why_clarity: Matches are exact, but whether a fragment infringes is ambiguous and disputes resolve slowly.
why_digital: Audio and video fingerprints matched and adjudicated in software.

why_ai: Explaining and stabilising rule-driven income is modelling and product work.
why_clarity: Income per video is an exact figure, but suitability rules shift without notice.
why_digital: Suitability classifications and revenue shares computed and paid online.

why_ai: Localising what triggered a classifier is a capability inside existing models.
why_clarity: Every decision needs an explanation, but faithfulness of explanations is hard to verify.
why_digital: Model internals and video content in, explanations out.

why_ai: Enforcement is automated by necessity; contestability and regulatory accountability keep some humans involved.
why_clarity: Huge decision volume, but removal and suppression correctness are seldom checked.
why_digital: Classifiers act on uploaded video and creators are notified online.

why_ai: Real-time moderation and monetisation of live broadcasts must be automated because no human can keep pace.
why_clarity: Continuous real-time decisions, with fuzzy policy lines and little review afterwards.
why_digital: Live video and chat streams handled entirely by platform systems.

why_ai: Deciding automatically everything that does not need a person uses models already in the building.
why_clarity: The share auto-decided and the exposure reduced per reviewer are directly measurable.
why_digital: Flagged content in, filtered queues out.

why_ai: Recommenders are fully automated; the open question is the objective, not who does the work.
why_clarity: Watch time is instant, but whether viewers were glad has never been measured.
why_digital: Viewing logs in, ranked feeds out.

why_ai: Platforms' own models are shrinking the queue, leaving humans the escalated judgment calls.
why_clarity: Written policy guides a high-volume queue, but individual call accuracy is rarely audited.
why_digital: Outsourced reviewers work queues of digital content on screen.

why_ai: Top creators value the one person who answers; the relationship is the role's product.
why_clarity: Cases vary, and resolution depends on navigating opaque internal systems by experience.
why_digital: Cases handled by phone, email and dashboards, with occasional in-person creator events.
